raw_response:
The bug is in silver_transactions: txn_date is derived from ingest_ts instead of txn_ts. The ingest_ts is the day after the transaction (02:00 the next day), so every row is off by one day. All 4558 POSTED rows mismatch, which equals the number of silver rows. The fix is to derive txn_date from CAST(txn_ts AS DATE).

Whether the date should be taken from txn_ts is supported by the DATE_CONSISTENCY monitor and by the change note about refactoring the date derivation. The txn_ts values all look like 06:xx times, so there is no timezone ambiguity. Only silver_transactions needs replacing, since the gold tables are rebuilt from it.

Confidence is high.

{"diagnosis": "The DE-398 refactor made silver_transactions.txn_date come from ingest_ts (loaded the next day at 02:00) instead of txn_ts, so every row is off by one day. Deriving txn_date from CAST(txn_ts AS DATE) fixes silver and the downstream gold tables.", "decision": "fix", "confidence": 0.93, "pre_sql": [], "step_overrides": {"silver_transactions": "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE silver_transactions AS SELECT CAST(txn_id AS BIGINT) AS txn_id, customer_id, CAST(merchant_id AS INTEGER) AS merchant_id, CAST(amount AS DECIMAL(12,2)) AS amount, CAST(txn_ts AS TIMESTAMP) AS txn_ts, CAST(txn_ts AS DATE) AS txn_date FROM raw_transactions WHERE status = 'POSTED'"}}
